title: One rule, different beginnings.
prompt: Run the affine recurrence twice with different initial values. Then interpret what changed.
hint: Change x₀ between the two runs. Keep the same multiplier and offset.

conclusions.text: The recurrence alone selected a unique orbit, regardless of its initial value.
The same update rule can produce different sequences when initial values differ.
Two different orbits disprove the recurrence.

feedback.pass: Initial data is part of the experiment, not an optional footnote.
feedback.fail: Compare the initial states. The rule is the same; its orbit also depends on the starting value.
